claims.text: TypeSafe AI opened early access to Jev, their SystemOne model, in the week before this post (September 2026).
GeoDeploy compares every AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud region that offers managed Kubernetes.
TypeSafe's Jev provides AI primitives that let apps, agents, and workflows make decisions based on context.
Jev's decision-making primitives are confidence scoring, multiple choice, and yes/no (noul) questions.
GeoDeploy fetches current prices from the AWS Price List API, the Azure Retail Prices API, and the Google Cloud Billing Catalog.
GeoDeploy's module registry supports EKS, AKS, GKE; ECR, ACR, Artifact Registry; DNS via Route 53, NS1, or Cloudflare.
The Pulumi Automation API runs a preview and then an update, with one stack per region, and GeoDeploy won't run unless cloud credentials pass readiness checks.
Every GeoDeploy run writes plan.json and plan.md with the full decision record.
Jev's choice() returns the pick, a probability distribution across all options, and a confidence; score() rates against a rubric; noul() answers a yes/no question with a single probability.
GeoDeploy's score rubrics use 10 levels.
Jev only selects from closed sets and never writes code or does arithmetic, so hallucinated regions can't occur by construction.
GeoDeploy sends Jev a shortlist of up to 40 priced candidates per geo.
The @typesafe-ai/sdk package exports choice, noul, and score.
TypeSafe advises rubrics to "describe situations, not degrees."
TypeSafeClient exposes systemOne({state, questions}) returning answers with selection.choice, confidence, residencyOk.noul, and coverage.score.
GeoDeploy's ranking uses weight profiles: latency-optimized (default), balanced, residency-first, and failure-domain.

Weight profile values: latency-optimized cost 0.13, coverage 0.48, maturity 0.17, sprawl 0.1, arch 0.12; balanced 0.25/0.25/0.2/0.12/0.18; residency-first 0.12/0.12/0.38/0.23/0.15; failure-domain 0.08/0.17/0.48/0.15/0.12.
Cluster and registry modules follow from provider (AWS means EKS and ECR); Jev decides ingress posture, autoscaling posture, and node-pool sizing tier.

GeoDeploy confidence thresholds: data residency 0.95 hard reject; new cluster region 0.90 flags top three for human; existing stack region 0.75 keep existing; ingress/autoscaling module 0.85 registry default; node-pool tier 0.60 bin-packing result; global floor 0.50 drops AI path.
Each AiPathAborted carries the full attempt (state, questions, answers) so rejected answers land in the audit trail.
If a gate fails, the API times out or errors, or upstream is unreachable, GeoDeploy falls back to deterministic price comparison while enforcing residency and constraint checks.
`geodeploy explain` shows why each region won.

`geodeploy monitor` enables self-driving mode, which periodically checks CPU utilization and asks Jev one joint question with options no-change, scale-up, scale-down, shift, plus a disruption-risk check.
In self-driving mode, above 0.85 confidence the resize is applied automatically; between 0.70 and 0.85 it is suggested for human approval; below 0.70 a deterministic per-region rule is used.
CPU utilization alone is a poor autoscaling metric and is usually paired with other signals like latency and error rates.
GeoDeploy is open source at github.com/pulumi/devx-geodeploy.
The Pulumi Automation API page exists at /automation/.
